mentions.name: TTZ
mentions.description: TTZ is a next-generation terminal protocol providing a middle ground between web apps and terminal UIs. It supports raster images, vector graphics, simple audio, and file transfer, with client and server libraries implemented for multiple languages, so apps and workflows can move from heavyweight web apps to a lighter terminal-based experience.
mentions.problem: Web apps are too resource-heavy for low-spec machines (e.g., a 2 GB RAM laptop), while terminals and SSH have spotty image support, no audio, and limited vector graphics (ReGis) support.
mentions.source_excerpt:
I'm working on TTZ, a sort of, pardon the expression, next-gen terminal protocol.

I wanted a middle ground between web apps and Terminal UI that allows for things like raster images, vector graphics, simple audio support and file transfer; to let me move more apps and workflows from web apps to a lighter experience.
mentions.author: hexmiles
